newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to make coconut productivity blueprint.
newsitem.headline: Manila to make coconut productivity blueprint.

text.p: Philippine Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero on Tuesday unveiled plans to make a blue print to ensure the country remains the world's largest exporter of coconut products.
In a statement, Escudero said his agency plans to draw up a sensible and viable medium and long-term strategy to ensure adequate coconut seedlings and fertilisers to farmers.
The Philippine Coconut Authority has said coconut production fell to 2.2 million tonnes in 1996 after it reached an all-time high of three million tonnes in 1995.
Last year's coconut production was hurt by a series of typhoons that struck growing areas in late 1995.
Traders also blamed indiscriminate cutting of coconut trees to the drop in coconut harvests.
The Philippine is the major exporter of coconut products, particularly coconut oil to both the United States and Europe.

The Agriculture department said it plans to hold consultations with coconut farmers on government regulations on the cutting of coconut trees and the setting up of coconut oil mills and dessicated coconut plants.
Coconut farmers blamed the unabated establishment of coconut oil mills and dessicated coconut plants in the past several months to the drop in the domestic price of coconut products.
"We would carry out a scheme that will further protect and develop the coconut industry and the people depending on it for livelihood," Escudero said.
